data:
Written texts have long informed audio-visual media, whether as the basis of story, research or in more subtle ways. Cinema and photography also have a notable history of inspiring writers, and writers sometimes experiment with weaving visual elements into their writing in a manner where the photographs are not merely illustrations of the text, and the text does not simply caption the pictures. Instead, the reader experiences the integrated, mutually enhancing relationship created between text and image.

We will examine the history of this complicated and fruitful relationship between words and pictures, whether in books, in direct film adaptations or in inventive recreations. We will view different kinds of non-fiction films, from classic documentaries to more poetic and elliptical uses of the cinematic medium. Discussing and analysing these will widen the understanding of how words, both spoken and written, work when forming partnerships with moving images and sound.

Course Objectives / Learning Outcomes: Discussing and analysing these will widen the understanding of how words, both spoken and written, work when forming partnerships with moving images and sound.
